svg.text: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) – cross-AZ recovery of an EC2 server
Source subnet → continuous block replication to staging subnet → drill / recovery launched into recovery subnet → failover (and optional failback)
failover: users redirected to recovery server (DNS / Elastic IP)
1. Terraform: VPC + 3 subnets, source EC2, IAM users, DRS init + replication template (t3.small, gp2, 7-day PIT).
2. Replication Agent installed on source with IAM user keys → DRS starts a replication server and staging disks.
3. Initial sync → snapshot → status Ready; data replicates continuously on TCP 1500.
4. "Disaster" in AZ a → start drill/recovery from a point-in-time snapshot → conversion server → recovery server in AZ f.
5. Failover: redirect users to recovery server. Later failback via Failback Client, or keep the recovery server.
6. Cleanup: terminate recovery instance, disconnect + delete source server, delete leftovers, terraform destroy.
